/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 15 May 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3151 (-44)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5173 (-143)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2521 (18)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1565 (7)
Baltic Handysize Index: 850 (-1)
CAPESIZE
Following holidays across several countries yesterday, the week concluded on a notably subdued note, with activity across both basins lacking conviction and trading volumes thinning into the close. The BCI 182 5TC fell by $1,293 to settle at $46,916, reflecting the softer overall tone despite underlying support remaining in both basins. In the Pacific, conditions were generally steady but uninspiring, with limited fresh enquiry and reduced miner participation weighing on sentiment. Two C5 miners were initially reported in the market, although trading activity remained extremely thin throughout the session. C5 declined by 0.423 to $15.010, with market talk suggesting an overage vessel fixed at $14.90, and low $15s had been paid otherwise little concluded business emerged before the close. The Atlantic remained comparatively firmer structurally, particularly in the North Atlantic where tonnage continues to appear tight. South Brazil and West Africa to China business also retained underlying support, although activity levels were similarly limited. On C3, a widening gap developed for index dates, with bids reportedly around $36.50 against offers closer to $37.50, restricting liquidity. Nevertheless, $36.75 was again heard fixed for early June and 10/15 June laycans, helping keep the route relatively stable overall, with C3 easing marginally by $0.125 to $36.800.
PANAMAX
A quieter end to the week was observed compared to the flurry of activity seen earlier, with the P5TC improving by $163 to $22,691. The trans Atlantic market is said by brokers to be maintaining its positive sentiment, with higher levels continuing to be discussed. The North Atlantic has also been highlighted by some as looking slim in relation to the volume of offers being discussed. Fronthaul activity moved sideways today with brokers noting that following the European holidays and with it being Friday many market participants have stepped back to reassess conditions. In the Pacific, sentiment remains mixed. Some suggest that increasing tonnage supply may begin to outweigh cargo demand, while others maintain that activity across Indonesia, Australia, and the North Pacific remains healthy, supporting a positive outlook. Offers are generally being held at previous levels, creating a sense of stand-off in the market. Period activity has been active, with the ETG Aquarius (81,976 2022) open North China 1/10 June reportedly placed on subjects for short period with Mingwah. Meanwhile the Zhong Chang Zhou Shan (75,409 2013) open Gunsan 27/30 May, is also said to be on subjects for 5–7 months at $19,300, with the charterer undisclosed.

Atlantic
The Agios Georgios S (75,041 2012) open in Kandla 16/17 May has now been linked to Messrs Bunge for a trip via East Coast South America to Singapore-Japan at $19,500. Koch have been linked with the Risoluto (82,718 2025) open Gibraltar 23/25 May for a trip to the Far East with grains at $35,000.

Asia
The Adriatica Graeca II (82,000 2026) open in Zhoushan 16/17 May was discussed as being place on subjects but no further details have emerged.
SUPRAMAX
A typical slow end to the week after yesterday’s Ascension Day holiday, with many players in the Atlantic staying away from their desks. The South American market remained relatively firm with a good supply of fresh cargo brokers said, although fresh fixing information remained lacking. The US Gulf was balanced, whilst the Continent-Mediterranean lacked fresh impetus. The Asian arena saw mixed fortunes from an owners' perspective whilst the north remained in positive territory, brokers said the fresh enquiry was slowing further south which in turn was putting downward pressure on rates. The 11TC average did however remain in positive motion gaining a further $90 to finish at $19,788.

Atlantic
The Aquarius (56,048 2013) open EC Mexico fixed for a trip with grains basis delivery SW Pass trip West Mediterranean at $20,000 to Bunge. The HSL Mexico (61,167 2020) open Altamira fixed for a trip with grains again delivery SW Pass to Japan at $25,000 with MOL. Also, the Jade Wealth (64,301 2024) open Mississippi River fixed for trip with grains to EC Mexico at $19,000 to Ultrabulk.

Asia
Little fresh activity surfaced, but from the Indian Ocean the Allis Serene (58,098 2011) was heard fixed Goa 18/20 May trip via New Mangalore redelivery Mombasa at $18,000 to Team Bulk.

HANDYSIZE
It was a typical quiet Friday for the Handy sector, with minimal visible activity. The Baltic Handysize Index remained at 850 while the 7TC average down by $15, closed at $15,296. In the Continent and Mediterranean, market fundamentals and rate levels stayed largely unchanged. In the South Atlantic, the outlook continue to remain soft due a lengthy tonnage list and limited demand. Meanwhile, the U.S. Gulf appeared rather subdued, with no change in its fundamentals. In the Pacific, the market saw a slower day with owners were willing to wait as rates were trending upwards. Charterers with prompt cargoes were actively looking to cover them, however rates are being recorded around the last done levels.

Market Fundamentals
CISA Daily Crude Steel Production

After declining in late-April, daily crude steel production at Chinese Iron and Steel Association (CISA) member mills rose 3.6% from the preceding ten days to 2.1 Mt/day in the period 1-10 May, according to the industry association. However, output stood 4.3% below the same period last year. As of 10 May, finished steel inventories of large and medium-sized enterprises in China also rose, up 9.4% from end-April to 16.9 Mt. The rise in stocks was faster than the lift in daily crude steel output since the Labour Day holiday (1-5 May) resulted in slack demand from downstream users. In the week to 8 May, the percentage of profitable Blast Furnace steel mills climbed 9.1 percentage points from the prior week to 60.2%, the highest since September 2025, MySteel data show.

Meanwhile, Chinese iron ore imports lifted 0.7 Mt year-on-year to 103.8 Mt in April, despite lower shipments from Australia and heavy rain in Brazil.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve was well supported today despite the index coming off another $1293, however the Atlantic physical market remains very tight still. The biggest move was on the June contract with 38650 paid, followed by the July with 35050 trading. The move on May was still significant, reaching a top of 42600. The May v Jun spread narrowed and weakened as a result, back down to 4000. Buying interest on the Q3 was similarly strong with a range of 32850-33350 and the Q4 31750-32100, with the Q3 v Q4 spread widening out to 1300. The Cal27 lacked liquidity today with a few clips printing marginally weaker down to 26600, before strengthening in response to the Q34 move.

PMX
PMX saw a relatively busy session for a Friday after a bank holiday for many, with activity mainly focused around the front of the curve. May stuck at 21500 in over 300 clips, June was again the main point of interest, trading between 21600 and 22050 finishing the day around 21800. while July traded in a tighter 21000–21300 range. August saw lighter activity at 20550, with September trading between 19800 and 19900. Further out, Q3 moved 20300–20650 closing around 20500, while Q4 traded in a narrower 18500–18700 range. The back end remained steady with Cal 27 staying around 15500.

SMX + HANDY
The down trend continued on smx paper today as we ended the week on a bearish note. Jun traded from 18750 to 18400 while q3 went from 18200 to 17900. Jul also Despite the move on the front the back end struggled to lose value with cal 27 having a conference rate of 13500, the same rate that was trading yesterday. Q1 did drop to trade 12400 in the afternoon while 27/28 spread traded at 1000.

Market Fundamentals
CISA Daily Crude Steel Production
After declining in late-April, daily crude steel production at
Chinese Iron and Steel Association (CISA) member mills rose
3.6% from the preceding ten days to 2.1 Mt/day in the period
1-10 May, according to the industry association. However,
output stood 4.3% below the same period last year. As of 10
May, ﬁnished steel inventories of large and medium-sized
enterprises in China also rose, up 9.4% from end-April to 16.9
Mt. The rise in stocks was faster than the lift in daily crude
steel output since the Labour Day holiday (1-5 May) resulted
in slack demand from downstream users. In the week to 8
May, the percentage of proﬁtable Blast Furnace steel mills
climbed 9.1 percentage points from the prior week to 60.2%,
the highest since September 2025, MySteel data show.
Meanwhile, Chinese iron ore imports lifted 0.7 Mt year-on-
year to 103.8 Mt in April, despite lower shipments from
Australia and heavy rain in Brazil.
Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve was well supported today despite the
index coming oﬀ another $1293, however the Atlantic
physical market remains very tight still. The biggest move
was on the June contract with 38650 paid, followed by the
July with 35050 trading. The move on May was still
signiﬁcant, reaching a top of 42600. The May v Jun spread
narrowed and weakened as a result, back down to 4000.
Buying interest on the Q3 was similarly strong with a range
of 32850-33350 and the Q4 31750-32100, with the Q3 v Q4
spread widening out to 1300. The Cal27 lacked liquidity
today with a few clips printing marginally weaker down to
26600, before strengthening in response to the Q34 move.
PMX
PMX saw a relatively busy session for a Friday after a bank
holiday for many, with activity mainly focused around the
front of the curve. May stuck at 21500 in over 300 clips, June
was again the main point of interest, trading between 21600
and 22050 ﬁnishing the day around 21800. while July traded
in a tighter 21000–21300 range. August saw lighter activity at
20550, with September trading between 19800 and 19900.
Further out, Q3 moved 20300–20650 closing around 20500,
while Q4 traded in a narrower 18500–18700 range. The back
end remained steady with Cal 27 staying around 15500.
SMX + HANDY
The down trend continued on smx paper today as we ended
the week on a bearish note. Jun traded from 18750 to 18400
while q3 went from 18200 to 17900. Jul also Despite the
move on the front the back end struggled to lose value with
cal 27 having a conference rate of 13500, the same rate that
was trading yesterday. Q1 did drop to trade 12400 in the
afternoon while 27/28 spread traded at 1000.Cape 180 5TC

Capesize Report15th May 2026
Market Comments
A steady week in the Paciﬁc as demand in the basin held strong throughout the week as a healthy presence of majors in the basin gave conﬁdence to
owners, however activity was seen to be sparse. Monday reﬂected a false start in the basin, despite the presence of two majors. The Dampier major went
unﬁxed on Monday as they were unwilling to engage oﬀers in the low $15s region for their late May C5 stem. Out of Indonesia, the usual operator was
reported to be holding a $12 oﬀer for their stem to Mundra, but no further action was seen. It wasn’t until Tuesday that activity picked up with four majors
giving a lift in demand. However, majors seemed underwhelmed by the level of oﬀers in the low/mid $15s until the Dampier major took a handful of for
27/30 May at a $15.00-15 range. One German owner’s vessel was seen to ﬁx on a 05/14 June stem out of Newcastle to Taiwan in the mid-high $21s.
Additionally, the usual major out of Teluk ﬁxed their 25/27 May cargo on a trip to China in the very high $11s. One operator’s stem out of Peru to China for
24/28 May was linked to C3 index in the region of 3%. Finally, a miner out of Haypoint promptly ﬁxed an early June backhaul stem to Rotterdam in the high
$27s. Lastly, the usual operator out of Indonesia ﬁxed their 24/28 May repositioning cargo to Mundra in the mid $12s rounded oﬀ the day. Into mid-week,
the bulk of business was concluded on Wednesday before things began to quieten down into the tail end of the week. Owners continued to push on pricing
as oﬀers on the $16s were seen from the get-go pressuring the two present majors and peripheral C5 stems. A Hedland major was found wanting once
more, concluding the day unﬁxed despite the Dampier major ﬁxing a few stems for 28 May/01 June at a $15.75-80 range with a couple operators concluding
their C5 stems as well. Meanwhile, a Chinese operator ﬁxed their tender out of Newcastle on an early June trip to Putian in the low/mid $22’s. Demand
remained consistently strong as three majors were in the market on Thursday. Activity, however, began to decline with limited oﬀers being pushed by
owners. Majors were reluctant to entertain levels in the mid/high $15s, only the Dampier major engaged, bidding mid $14s vs low $15s oﬀered, but went
unﬁxed once again. One operator took a couple of split May/June C5 stems, though rates are unknown – which made up the bulk of activity on C5.
Meanwhile, the usual major out of TRMT ﬁxed their 27/29 May stem to Dung Quat in the mid $8s. Lastly, one Chinese operator ﬁxed a second tender for the
week in the mid $16s out of DBCT to Liuheng. On Friday, the presence of two Hedland majors kept demand strong in the Paciﬁc this Friday. One major was
quick to ﬁx at $14.90 for their 03/05 June C5 stem, whilst the other major secured their 29 May C5 stem at low $15's, respectively. Meanwhile, an operator
sought candidates for their 03/09 June stem from Samrinda to Mundra - however, remained unﬁxed. Overall, a slightly softer tone in the paciﬁc as the week
comes to a close.
A strong week in the South Atlantic had opened on Monday to a static start before peaking in activity across mid-week and ending on a strong positive tone
on Friday. Monday saw little activity, however one Korean end user’s 11/20 June tender ﬁxed in the high $33s from Ubu to Korea. Operators’ bids soon
disregarded this rate as owners claimed to see strong levels from the get-go in the mid $35.00’s region for early/mid June tonnage, while oﬀers stood in the
$37.00’s setting up the week for strong activity. Focus held on early/mid June dates throughout the week in the South Atlantic as activity soared on Tuesday
afternoon. Owners were determined to ﬁx as oﬀers at $37 C3 for early and mid June tonnage were prominent, whilst bids sat £1.50 below. A volley of
ﬁxtures were soon seen to ﬁx into the afternoon as a handful of mid June C3 stems ﬁxed at a $36.50-37.00 C3 range. A few earlier C3 stems for 06/12 June
ﬁxed at a $36.50-85 C3 range, whilst one trader agreed their C3 stem for $36.25 C3 – with the peak of the day being a Greek owners vessel ﬁxing for 13/20
June around $37 C3. Into Wednesday, the basin saw much lower levels of activity as a healthy volume of cargo was cleared on Tuesday, though demand
remained strong in the South Atlantic. A Newcastlemax ﬁxed promptly on one trader's stem from Itaguai to China for 11/17 June at $36.25 C3, whilst $37.25
C3 was achieved in the afternoon on once operator’s stem for 08/10 June. Owners continued to drive the market and pushed oﬀers into the afternoon in the
mid $37.00's and more across early June dates, though with few bids shown, operator presence was limited. However, one operator ﬁxed their cargo to India
from South Africa in the very high $17s for 01/10 June. It became clear on Thursday that the operators’ enthusiasm was waning after the signiﬁcant levels
achieved earlier in the week. Owners remained consistent on price for early/mid June dates, standing at mid $37s C3 whilst oﬀers for forward end June sat
slightly lower. A Newcastlemax ﬁxed on a second stem from Itaguai to Qingdao for 18/20 June in the low $37s C3, whilst one operator ﬁxed their C3 stem on
a German owner’s ship for 10/15 June at $37.25 C3. Into Friday morning, early activity kicked oﬀ the ﬁnal day of the week as one trader’s 06/10 June C3 stem
ﬁxed at $36.75, whilst a Chinese operator’s cargo for similar dates ﬁxed in the mid/high $36s C3. Owners were oﬀering a $37.00-50 range, whilst one trader
was seen bidding $36.75 as demand in the South continues to remain strong across early/mid June dates, setting up strong levels of activity into next week.
The week rounded oﬀ with a tender out of Saldanha bay ﬁxing to an operator at $27.19 for 10/14 Jun to China.
The North continued to see strong demand throughout the week which was supported by high volumes of activity and a moderate tonnage. Monday saw
one end user’s fronthaul tender from Narvik to Kandla ﬁxed on a German operator’s vessel for 19/28 May at $43.50, which ran to 73.5k over 65 days and a
$2.15mil score equivalent to $83k C9. Additionally, one operator ﬁxed a couple of their transatlantic stems to start the week, from Nouadhibou to Arzew for
tight end May dates in the high $12s which ran to around $56k adjusted for C8 duration as well as an Acu to Arzew cargo for 01/10 June. Tuesday saw one
operator’s fronthaul stem from Drummond to South Korea holding a $48 oﬀer for end June dates, but still remained, overall West African stems remained
lucrative to North Atlantic stationed vessels. Demand continued to hold strong into an active Wednesday as one German owner was seen to make up the
bulk of activity as they took a couple of stems. Fixing one backhaul cargo out of Saldanha Bay to Rotterdam for mid June at $17.00 which ran to around very
low $20k's and a $1.42mil score for 65 day duration. Additionally, the same operator took a transatlantic stem for 20/29 May dates from Canada to France at
a reported mid $22.50, which runs to around $56.7k as a Gibraltar RV. Momentum carried through into Thursday after the usual major out of Brazil promptly
ﬁxed their cargo at high $27.00's. On a transatlantic round voyage to Misurata for 08/17 June this ran to mid $40k's as a Gib RV, while on a ballaster this ran
to around $16k adjusted. As the week came to a close on Friday, one miner’s fronthaul stem from Sept-Iles to China for forward late June dates attracted
welcomed interest from moderate North tonnage. The basin continued to feel positive as demand remains strong and tonnage moderate heading into next
week.

WHILE A STRONG PACIFIC MARKET CONTINUES TO DISCOURAGE BALLASTING. ALTHOUGH SOME
PROMPT VESSELS OPEN OVER THE WEEKEND HAVE SHOWN MORE FLEXIBILITY, THE OVERALL
SUPPLY/DEMAND BALANCE REMAINS SUPPORTIVE. PROVIDED CAPES HOLD THEIR RECENT GAINS
AND CARGO FLOW REMAINS STEADY, THE ATLANTIC SHOULD CONTINUE TO TRADE AT ELEVATED
LEVELS INTO NEXT WEEK, THOUGH AFTER THE RECENT SHARP MOVE HIGHER A PERIOD OF
CONSOLIDATION WOULD NOT BE SURPRISING.
PAC SHORT:

REMAINING STRONGLY POSITIVE ON THE BACK OF HEALTHY CARGO ACTIVITY AND AGGRESSIVE
FIXING ACROSS MOST ROUTES. EARLY IN THE WEEK, CARGO VOLUMES IMPROVED ACROSS THE
BASIN WHILE TONNAGE REMAINED RELATIVELY BALANCED DESPITE A SLIGHT INCREASE IN
AVAILABLE VESSELS, ALLOWING OWNERS TO MAINTAIN STRONG LEVERAGE. AUSSIE ROUNDS LED

STRENGTHENED STEADILY WITH FRESH GRAIN AND COAL DEMAND SUPPORTING RATES. P3
CLIMBED SHARPLY THROUGH THE FIRST HALF OF THE WEEK AND WAS SEEN FIXING AROUND THE
$24/25,000 LEVEL, WHILE P5 ALSO CONTINUED TO POST GAINS ALONGSIDE THE BROADER PACIFIC
RALLY. HOWEVER, BY MIDWEEK ONWARDS, MOMENTUM BEGAN TO FADE AS CARGO ENQUIRY
SLOWED NOTICEABLY ACROSS MOST REGIONS AND CHARTERERS STARTED PULLING BACK AFTER
THE SHARP RUN UP IN RATES. FFAS ALSO TURNED SOFTER ACROSS THE CURVE DURING THE
LATTER PART OF THE WEEK, REFLECTING GROWING CAUTION AROUND WHETHER THE MARKET
COULD SUSTAIN SUCH ELEVATED LEVELS. ALTHOUGH INDICES REMAINED POSITIVE, DESPITE THE
SOFTER SENTIMENT SEEN TOWARDS THE END OF THE WEEK, THE MARKET CONTINUED TO HOLD
RELATIVELY FIRM OVERALL, WITH RATES MANAGING TO MAINTAIN MOST OF THE GAINS ACHIEVED
EARLIER IN THE WEEK. ON THE SUPPLY SIDE, TONNAGE REMAINED RELATIVELY CONTROLLED,
THOUGH THE BALANCE GRADUALLY BEGAN LOOSENING LATER IN THE WEEK AS CARGOES PUSHED
FURTHER FORWARD AND FRESH ENQUIRY REMAINED LIMITED COMPARED TO FIRST HALF OF THE

Panam ax/Kam sarm ax Report15th May 2026
Atlantic Comment
NORTH ATLANTIC:
THE ATLANTIC MARKET EXTENDED ITS GAINS THROUGH MIDWEEK, DRIVEN BY STRONGER CAPES, FIRM PACIFIC SUPPORT AND A TIGHT TONNAGE LIST ACROSS BOTH THE NORTH
AND SOUTH ATLANTIC. OWNERS REMAINED FIRMLY IN CONTROL THROUGH WEDNESDAY, THOUGH A QUIETER END TO THE WEEK DUE TO ASCENSION DAY HOLIDAYS ACROSS
EUROPE TOOK SOME MOMENTUM OUT OF THE MARKET AND LED TO MORE CAUTIOUS POSITIONING INTO THE WEEKEND.
1A
THE TRANSATLANTIC MARKET SAW A SHARP RE-RATING THROUGH THE FIRST HALF OF THE WEEK, AS TIGHT TONNAGE AND STRONGER CAPE EARNINGS FORCED CHARTERERS TO
PAY UP FOR PROMPT COVER. SHORTER MINERAL TRANSATLANTIC RUNS WERE CONCLUDED AS HIGH AS USD 24,000 BKI EQUIVALENT EX ALGECIRAS, WHILE LONGER DURATION TA
BUSINESS TRADED MOSTLY IN THE MID USD 22,000’S TO LOW USD 23,000’S. ACTIVITY LEVELS WERE HEALTHY THROUGH WEDNESDAY, WITH OWNERS PUSHING OFFERS HIGHER
AFTER EACH REPORTED FIXTURE. HOWEVER, AS THE WEEK PROGRESSED INTO THURSDAY, MOMENTUM SLOWED AND SOME VESSELS OPENING OVER THE WEEKEND BECAME
MORE FLEXIBLE ON IDEAS IN ORDER TO SECURE COVER. EVEN SO, THE TONNAGE LIST REMAINS RELATIVELY TIGHT, AND THE MARKET CLOSES THE WEEK WELL ABOVE LAST
FRIDAY’S LEVELS.
2A
FRONTHAUL REMAINED THE STRONGEST ROUTE IN THE BASIN THIS WEEK. NCSA GRAINS CONTINUED TO DOMINATE THE MARKET, WHILE ADDITIONAL DEMAND FROM THE US
INTO INDIA AND THE FAR EAST PROVIDED FURTHER SUPPORT. WITH VERY FEW SUITABLE VESSELS AVAILABLE, OWNERS WERE ABLE TO PUSH LEVELS AGGRESSIVELY HIGHER
THROUGH MIDWEEK. WE SAW MULTIPLE NCSA/FEAST FIXTURES CONCLUDED AROUND USD 31,000 BKI EQUIVALENT EX ALGECIRAS, WHILE A PROMPT USEC/INDIA RUN WAS
REPORTED AS HIGH AS USD 34,000 BKI EQUIVALENT EX ALGECIRAS. VOLUME WAS DECENT THROUGH THE FIRST HALF OF THE WEEK AND THE MARKET LOOKED GENUINELY TIGHT.
HOWEVER, THE HOLIDAY SHORTENED END TO THE WEEK REDUCED LIQUIDITY AND A FEW PROMPT VESSELS OPEN OVER THE WEEKEND WERE REPORTED MORE NEGOTIABLE ON
OFFERS. DESPITE THIS, THE UNDERLYING BALANCE REMAINS SUPPORTIVE WITH LIMITED TONNAGE AVAILABLE FOR MAY/1H JUNE DATES.
P6
THE SOUTH ATLANTIC ALSO CONTINUED TO FIRM, THOUGH ACTIVITY LEVELS WERE MORE MEASURED COMPARED TO THE NORTH ATLANTIC. FIXTURES WERE REPORTED IN THE
LOW TO MID USD 22,000’S P6 EQUIVALENT, WITH OWNERS BENEFITTING FROM A THIN BALLASTER LIST AND CONTINUED PACIFIC STRENGTH PREVENTING AN INFLUX OF OPEN
TONNAGE. WHILE THE MARKET CONTINUES TO MOVE HIGHER, DEPTH OF BUYING HAS BEEN LESS IMPRESSIVE THAN IN PREVIOUS WEEKS. IN ADDITION, ULTRAMAX TONNAGE
REMAINS COMPETITIVE, ALLOWING CHARTERERS WITH FLEXIBILITY TO SOURCE GEARED TONNAGE AT LOWER LEVELS. NEVERTHELESS, THE OVERALL SUPPLY SIDE REMAINS WELL
MANAGED, AND THERE IS LITTLE SIGN OF OWNERS LOSING CONFIDENCE AT CURRENT LEVELS.

Panam ax/Kam sarm ax Report15th May 2026
Paciﬁc Comment
PAC LONG:
THE NOPAC MARKET PERFORMED STEADILY THROUGHOUT THE WEEK AND WAS ONE OF THE KEY SUPPORTIVE FACTORS BEHIND THE PACIFIC RALLY DURING THE EARLY STAGES.
FRESH GRAIN AND COAL STEMS FOR EARLY JUNE, ALONGSIDE SOME REMAINING END MAY CARGOES, HELPED PUSH RATES HIGHER AND ALLOWED P3 TO ACHIEVE AROUND THE
$24,000 LEVELS. HOWEVER, AS THE WEEK PROGRESSED, ENQUIRY BEGAN MOVING FURTHER FORWARD INTO MID-JUNE DATES AND THE AMOUNT OF FRESH CIRCULATION
SLOWED. WHILE TONNAGE IN THE NORTH REDUCED TOWARDS THE END OF THE WEEK, THE SLOWER PACE OF FRESH DEMAND AND INCREASINGLY CAUTIOUS CHARTERER
SENTIMENT RESULTED IN THE MARKET LOSING SOME MOMENTUM AFTER ITS STRONG START.
AUSTRALIA WAS UNDOUBTEDLY THE STRONGEST PERFORMING REGION, WITH AGGRESSIVE FIXING ACTIVITY AND TIGHT PROMPT DEMAND DRIVING RATES SHARPLY HIGHER.
EAUS ROUNDS ACHIEVED PREMIUM LEVELS, SUPPORTED BY STRONG EARLY JUNE DEMAND AND LIMITED PROMPT SUPPLY. HOWEVER, THE MARKET COOLED NOTICEABLY FROM
MIDWEEK ONWARDS AS THE STRONG SECOND HALF MAY MOMENTUM FAILED TO PROPERLY ROLL INTO JUNE. FRESH CARGO ENQUIRY BECAME INCREASINGLY THIN, WITH
ACTIVITY MAINLY LIMITED TO A HANDFUL OF CHINA STEMS FOR EARLY JUNE LAYCANS. DESPITE RATES REMAINING ELEVATED, SENTIMENT SOFTENED CONSIDERABLY AS
CHARTERERS STEPPED BACK AND ADOPTED A MORE CAUTIOUS WAIT-AND-SEE APPROACH AFTER THE RAPID RISE SEEN EARLIER IN THE WEEK.
INDO SAW SOME IMPROVEMENT AT THE START OF THE WEEK COMPARED TO PREVIOUS WEEKS, PARTICULARLY FOR LATER MAY DATES. HOWEVER, THE MARKET GRADUALLY LOST
MOMENTUM THROUGH THE SECOND HALF OF THE WEEK AS INDONESIAN COAL ENQUIRY SLOWED SIGNIFICANTLY, ESPECIALLY INTO SOUTHEAST ASIA. CHINESE COAL TRADING
ALSO BECAME QUIETER AMID VOLATILITY IN THE UNDERLYING COMMODITY MARKET, FURTHER WEIGHING ON SENTIMENT. BY FRIDAY, INDO DEMAND SEEMED THIN OVERALL,
WITH FRESH CARGO COUNT REMAINING WELL BELOW LEVELS SEEN IN RECENT WEEKS.
OVERALL, WHILE THE PACIFIC MARKET MANAGED TO HOLD ONTO MOST OF THE GAINS ACHIEVED EARLIER IN THE WEEK, THE BASIN CLEARLY LOST STEAM DURING THE LATTER
HALF AS CARGO ENQUIRY SLOWED AND CHARTERERS RESISTED HIGHER LEVELS. UNDERLYING COAL FUNDAMENTALS REMAIN SUPPORTIVE, BUT WITH QUIETER CARGO VOLUMES,
FLATTER FFAS AND INCREASINGLY CAUTIOUS SENTIMENT, THE MARKET LOOKS SET TO ENTER NEXT WEEK ON A MORE STABLE AND QUIETER FOOTING RATHER THAN CONTINUING
THE SHARP UPWARD TRAJECTORY SEEN AT THE START OF THIS WEEK. THAT SAID, EVEN WITH SOFTER SENTIMENT DEVELOPING TOWARDS THE END OF THE WEEK, THE MARKET
HAS STILL MANAGED TO HOLD ONTO ITS ELEVATED LEVELS RELATIVELY WELL, SUGGESTING UNDERLYING SUPPORT REMAINS FIRMLY IN PLACE FOR NOW.

Handysize/Supramax Report15th May 2026
63,500 Atlantic: FLAT      Paciﬁc: FLAT           38,000 Atlantic: FLAT      Paciﬁc: FLAT
Atlantic Comment
The Baltic Dry Index (BDI) shattered the 3,000-point barrier this week, reaching 3,189 by
Wednesday, its highest level since late 2023. This rally is driven by a massive surge in
Capesize earnings, which jumped over 5% to break $44,000 per day as miners aggressively
push supply from the Atlantic. However, the market is becoming increasingly two tiered,
while Capes are thriving, we are seeing limited cargoes on our segment as ports like
Kamsar now ship primarily on Capes for fronthaul movements. Bunker prices continue to
be a total rollercoaster, with VLSFO nearing the $1,000 threshold before swinging on volatile
crude shifts, keeping a tight squeeze on margins. Despite this, the outlook through June
remains ﬁrm, supported by double digit growth in global grain volumes and a recovery in
coal demand as a hot Asian summer and weak monsoon loom. While a tactical ceiling from
Panamax splits may soon cap the Capesize rally, the strong supply-push in iron ore and the
ramp-up at Simandou should maintain sentiment until the usual seasonal lull in July.
In the Mediterranean, we continue seeing a lack of fresh cargo enquiry. However, we are
starting to observe a slight improvement across most routes both in E.Med and W.Med,
with the latter showing somewhat ﬁrmer sentiment, likely supported by the stronger ECSA
market, which currently oﬀers more attractive returns despite the longer ballast distance.
On the other hand, levels in the Continent remain healthier compared to the Med. However,
this week we have seen some softening in the market due to the lack of fresh cargoes
around, particularly scrap, which has put some pressure on rates.
Unlike the resilient and ﬁrm Ultramax segment, the East Coast South America (ECSA)
Handysize market has become increasingly fragmented this week, with ﬁxture levels
varying wildly. This lack of clear direction has resulted in a two-tier market where rates are
dictated more by speciﬁc laycan dates and individual owner urgency than by any uniﬁed
regional trend. With fewer active cargoes to absorb the remaining tonnage, the previous
momentum has stalled, forcing a disconnect between those holding for last-done levels
and those ﬁxing lower to avoid becoming prompt.
The ECSA Supramax market remains ﬁrm this week, but owners are ﬁnding themselves
walking a tightrope between maintaining high benchmarks and overplaying their hand.
There is a growing awareness that if Supramax owners pull the rope too much, the rate
spread will narrow to the point where Panamax vessels become the more economical
choice for charterers, potentially triggering a shift in vessel preference. This thin balance is
further complicated by a widening discrepancy in earnings potential between vessel types;
while Eco Ultramaxes are commanding a signiﬁcant premium on Fronthaul runs compared
to standard Supramaxes, the Transatlantic market remains a strong where both types
continue to enjoy robust elevated levels.
A tale of 2 halves this week.... With the Ascension day holiday yesterday the market ground
to a halt, and today has been very quiet across the Atlantic basin. The USEC saw noticeably
more activity with coal cargos leading the charge, its either feast of famine on that coast
and it was a carbon feast this week. Runs to the Eastern Mediterranean proving the most
lucrative given the weak state of the market there. Ultramax vessels have been ﬁxing in the
upper 20's in the latter part of this week. The USG has been somewhat quieter, levels have
remained ﬂat but well supported. A 61 dwt ﬁxed a Japan grains at 25,000 midweek, and
owners continue to ask for same levels for clean FH cargos with end May/June dates. Local
grain runs in the have come oﬀ slightly. 19-21,000 usd per day can be achieved subject to
redel port, perhaps indicating owners willingness to stay in the area with the expectation of
a ﬁrmer June. Decent sentiment await us next week for a possible end May push which
we've seen in the previous months end.

Handysize/Supramax Report15th May 2026
Paciﬁc Comments
This week, the Paciﬁc Supramax market remained relatively stable overall. Although the pace of the rally has moderated compared to the previous sharp run-up, the overall market structure
remained healthy, with freight levels continuing to hold at elevated levels. Far East exports and the period market stayed active, providing solid support to the overall market, while the
Southeast Asian coal sector remained relatively ﬂat, though ﬁxture levels continued to stay ﬁrm.
The Indonesian coal market was relatively quiet this week, with limited fresh cargoes entering the market. However, as available tonnage in the region did not increase signiﬁcantly, freight levels
remained generally stable without any meaningful correction. Indo/SE Asia continued to be the most active regional route, with reported ﬁxtures including a UMX open Singapore ﬁxing around
USD 19k for Indo/Philippines, and another UMX open Singapore ﬁxing around USD 20.5k for Indo/Thai, indicating that short-haul coal trades continued to provide strong support. On the
Indo/China route, Supramax demand remained relatively limited, as part of the cargo ﬂow was handled by Panamax vessels, resulting in fewer visible ﬁxtures in the market. Activity on the
Indo/India route also softened slightly this week, with some owners preferring to keep their vessels within the Paciﬁc basin in anticipation of stronger Far East export and period opportunities.
The North Vietnam and South China region remained active this week. Long-haul cargoes such as clinker to Bangladesh and West Africa, as well as cement to the US Gulf and West Coast Central
America, continued to provide stable support to the regional market. Reported ﬁxtures included an SMX open South China ﬁxing above USD 22k for clinker to Bangladesh, and a UMX open
South China ﬁxing above USD 24k for limestone to Bangladesh. For other long-haul trades, charterers increasingly showed preference for securing tonnage through period employment, with
UMX short period levels in the South China–CJK area generally maintained above USD 21k. The nickel ore market was less active compared to previous weeks, with the overall pace of ﬁxtures
slowing somewhat, though shipment volumes remained steady.
The NOPAC market also maintained a reasonable level of activity. Supported by strong northern export demand, freight levels remained ﬁrm. Market reports included a UMX on subs above USD
20k for a NOPAC round voyage, as well as a UMX open North China ﬁxing around USD 19k for NOPAC round employment, indicating that market support remained solid.
North China steel and general cargo exports continued to perform strongly. With tonnage in the Far East remaining tight, freight levels stayed elevated. General cargo demand to West Africa
remained ﬁrm, with reports of a UMX open North China ﬁxing around USD 24.5k dop to WAFR. Steel exports to Southeast Asia also maintained healthy levels, with rates generally staying within
the high teens range, reﬂecting continued positive sentiment in the market.
The Australian market remained stable this week, with cargo supply continuing to be released at a regular pace. Grain and salt from Western Australia, coal from Eastern Australia, and minerals
from Northern Australia continued to move steadily, providing ongoing support to the regional market. Reported ﬁxtures included a UMX open Cigading ﬁxing around USD 22k+ for
Australia/China iron ore, as well as an eco UMX ﬁxing around USD 23k+ for Australia/China salt, with overall freight levels remaining ﬁrm.
In the period market, conﬁdence remained supported by the continued strength in the paper market. Although the spot market showed some signs of slowing, period levels remained ﬁrm
overall. UMX short period ﬁxing levels were generally maintained within the USD 21k–22k range, depending on vessel position, age, and speciﬁcations, reﬂecting owners’ continued conﬁdence
in the near- to medium-term market outlook.
Overall, although the Paciﬁc Supramax market did not continue the aggressive upward momentum seen previously, the underlying market structure has not weakened materially. Regional
tonnage supply remains relatively tight, while Far East export demand and period activity continue to provide strong support. In the near term, with no signiﬁcant inﬂow of open tonnage and
cargo volumes remaining stable, the market is expected to continue trading at elevated levels.

Price levels continue to soften slightly in the Indian Sub -Continent, with India
once again suffering more so than their counterparts as domestic steel de-
mand has weakened, resulting in inventory stockpiles at a number of recy-
cling facilities until market conditions improve. The weakness of the Rupee,
which recently hit an all -time low against the US Dollar before recovering
slightly, has further added pressure to sentiment from the Indian recyclers. At
the same time, firm freight earnings continue to discourage owners from re-
leasing older tonnage for recycling, keeping the supply of candidates limited.

The situation is similar in Bangladesh, where local scrap levels have dropped
by approximately USD 10 per lwt over the past week and, notably, closer to
USD 30 per lwt during the course of the past month. Consequently, this has
resulted in a more cautious sentiment being adopted by the ship recyclers.
The recent heavy rains have also had an immediate effect on activity at the
recycling yards and, with the monsoon season due to commence in earnest in
the coming weeks, it is expected that current levels may remain stable alt-
hough a softer demand environment could emerge should weather disrup-
tions intensify. Even so, underlying appetite from the leading HKC -compliant
yards remains present.

Pakistan continues to be the most aggressive in terms of striving to acquire
tonnage, as this sector is suffering from a shortage of imported scrap tradi-
tionally supplied from the Gulf region. This has created a stronger require-
ment internally although, in reality, there remains a shortage of buyers willing,
or able, to increase price levels sufficiently enough to draw tonnage away
from the Bangladesh market.

With the monsoon delivery window gradually narrowing across the Sub -
Continent, timing is also becoming an increasing consideration for both buy-
ers and sellers alike.

The vast majority of reported transactions are once again older sales, with
various different countries being the recipients. Fresh sales are limited to the
LPG carrier “Gas Crusader” (1,526 lwt), which has been committed for deliv-
ery to Bangladesh at a reported level of USD 550 per lwt, a price clearly signi-
fying the vessel’s high, albeit undisclosed, non -ferrous content. In addition,
the Drillship “Valaris DPS -1” (38,568 lwt) has been sold on an as is basis in
Indonesia on private terms. Geographically, Bangladesh remains the closest
recycling destination, however the vast majority of offshore units continue to
find their way towards India despite the considerably longer voyage, primarily
due to the stronger appetite and specialist capabilities available within that
sector.

Australia’s Clean Oil Product Imports Fall To One -Year Low In March
Australia’s clean oil product imports declined by 120K b/d m -o-m to 780K b/d in March, a one -year low, according to Australian P e-
troleum Statistics. Diesel imports fell by 110K b/d m -o-m to 440K b/d, the lowest since February 2025, while arrivals of jet fue l also
decreased by 30K b/d m -o-m to 130K b/d. Refinery throughput rose by 20K b/d m -o-m to 280K b/d, a three -month high.

CISA Daily Crude Steel Production
After declining in late -April, daily crude steel production at Chinese Iron and Steel Association (CISA) member mills rose 3.6% from
the preceding ten days to 2.1 Mt/day in the period 1 -10 May, according to the industry association. However, output stood 4.3% b e-
low the same period last year. As of 10 May, finished steel inventories of large and medium -sized enterprises in China also rose , up
9.4% from end -April to 16.9 Mt. The rise in stocks was faster than the lift in daily crude steel output since the Labour Day hol iday (1 -
5 May) resulted in slack demand from downstream users. In the week to 8 May, the percentage of profitable Blast Furnace steel
mills climbed 9.1 percentage points from the prior week to 60.2%, the highest since September 2025, MySteel data show. Mean-
while, Chinese iron ore imports lifted 0.7 Mt year -on-year to 103.8 Mt in April, despite lower shipments from Australia and heav y rain
in Brazil.

items.parsed_text: Capesize Report15th May 2026 PAC: Balanced ATL: Strong Market Comments The presence of two Hedland majors kept demand strong in the Pacific this Friday. One major was quick to fix at $14.90 for their 03/05 June C5 stem, whilst the other major fixed their 29 May C5 stem in the low $15s, respectively. Meanwhile, an operator sought candidates for their 03/09 June stem from Samrinda to Mundra - however, remained unfixed. Overall, a slightly softer tone in the Pacific as the week comes to a close. The South Atlantic remains active heading into the weekend as a few late week fixtures keep the basin firm. A German owner’s vessel fixed at $37.25 C3 on a mid June stem to China yesterday afternoon. Into this morning, early activity kicked off the final day of the week as one trader’s 06/10 June C3 stem fixed at $36.75, whilst a Chinese operator’s cargo for similar dates fixed in the mid/high $36s C3. Demand in the South continues to remain strong across early/mid June dates as owners offered a $37.00-50 range, whilst one trader was seen bidding $36.75. Into the afternoon, activity picked up with one miner’s tender from Saldanha Bay to China fixing for mid June at $27.19. The North Atlantic continues to be busy as the usual major out of Brazil promptly fixed their cargo at high $27.00's yesterday. On a transatlantic round voyage to Misurata for 08/17 June this ran to mid $40k's as a Gib RV, while on a ballaster this ran to around $16k adjusted. Into this morning, one miner’s fronthaul stem from Sept-Iles to China for forward late June dates attracts welcomed interest from moderate North tonnage. The basin continues to feel positive heading into next week as demand remains strong and tonnage moderate. Monday reflected a false start in the basin, despite the presence of two majors. The Dampier major went unfixed on Monday as they were unwilling to engage offers in the low $15s region for their late May C5 stem. Out of Indonesia, the usual operator was reported to be holding a $12 offer for their stem to Mundra, but no further action was seen. It wasn’t until Tuesday that activity picked up with four majors giving a lift in demand. However, majors seemed underwhelmed by the level of offers in the low/mid $15s until the Dampier major took a handful of for 27/30 May at a $15.00-15 range. One German owner’s vessel was seen to fix on a 05/14 June stem out of Newcastle to Taiwan in the mid-high $21s. Additionally, the usual major out of Teluk fixed their 25/27 May cargo on a trip to China in the very high $11s. One operator’s stem out of Peru to China for 24/28 May was linked to C3 index in the region of 3%. Finally, a miner out of Haypoint promptly fixed an early June backhaul stem to Rotterdam in the high $27s. Lastly, the usual operator out of Indonesia fixed their 24/28 May repositioning cargo to Mundra in the mid $12s rounded off the day. Into mid-week, the bulk of business was concluded on Wednesday before things began to quieten down into the tail end of the week. Owners continued to push on pricing as offers on the $16s were seen from the get-go pressuring the two present majors and peripheral C5 stems. A Hedland major was found wanting once more, concluding the day unfixed despite the Dampier major fixing a few stems for 28 May/01 June at a $15.75-80 range with a couple operators concluding their C5 stems as well. Meanwhile, a Chinese operator fixed their tender out of Newcastle on an early June trip to Putian in the low/mid $22’s. Demand remained consistently strong as three majors were in the market on Thursday. Activity, however, began to decline with limited offers being pushed by owners. Majors were reluctant to entertain levels in the mid/high $15s, only the Dampier major engaged, bidding mid $14s vs low $15s offered, but went unfixed once again. One operator took a couple of split May/June C5 stems, though rates are unknown – which made up the bulk of activity on C5. Meanwhile, the usual major out of TRMT fixed their 27/29 May stem to Dung Quat in the mid $8s. Lastly, one Chinese operator fixed a second tender for the week in the mid $16s out of DBCT to Liuheng. On Friday, the presence of two Hedland majors kept demand strong in the Pacific this Friday. One major was quick to fix at $14.90 for their 03/05 June C5 stem, whilst the other major secured their 29 May C5 stem at low $15's, respectively. Meanwhile, an operator sought candidates for their 03/09 June stem from Samrinda to Mundra - however, remained unfixed. Overall, a slightly softer tone in the pacific as the week comes to a close. A strong week in the South Atlantic had opened on Monday to a static start before peaking in activity across mid-week and ending on a strong positive tone on Friday. Monday saw little activity, however one Korean end user’s 11/20 June tender fixed in the high $33s from Ubu to Korea. Operators’ bids soon disregarded this rate as owners claimed to see strong levels from the get-go in the mid $35.00’s region for early/mid June tonnage, while offers stood in the $37.00’s setting up the week for strong activity. Focus held on early/mid June dates throughout the week in the South Atlantic as activity soared on Tuesday afternoon. Owners were determined to fix as offers at $37 C3 for early and mid June tonnage were prominent, whilst bids sat £1.50 below. A volley of fixtures were soon seen to fix into the afternoon as a handful of mid June C3 stems fixed at a $36.50-37.00 C3 range. A few earlier C3 stems for 06/12 June fixed at a $36.50-85 C3 range, whilst one trader agreed their C3 stem for $36.25 C3 – with the peak of the day being a Greek owners vessel fixing for 13/20 June around $37 C3. Into Wednesday, the basin saw much lower levels of activity as a healthy volume of cargo was cleared on Tuesday, though demand remained strong in the South Atlantic. A Newcastlemax fixed promptly on one trader's stem from Itaguai to China for 11/17 June at $36.25 C3, whilst $37.25 C3 was achieved in the afternoon on once operator’s stem for 08/10 June. Owners continued to drive the market and pushed offers into the afternoon in the mid $37.00's and more across early June dates, though with few bids shown, operator presence was limited. However, one operator fixed their cargo to India from South Africa in the very high $17s for 01/10 June. It became clear on Thursday that the operators’ enthusiasm was waning after the significant levels achieved earlier in the week. Owners remained consistent on price for early/mid June dates, standing at mid $37s C3 whilst offers for forward end June sat slightly lower. A Newcastlemax fixed on a second stem from Itaguai to Qingdao for 18/20 June in the low $37s C3, whilst one operator fixed their C3 stem on a German owner’s ship for 10/15 June at $37.25 C3. Into Friday morning, early activity kicked off the final day of the week as one trader’s 06/10 June C3 stem fixed at $36.75, whilst a Chinese operator’s cargo for similar dates fixed in the mid/high $36s C3. Owners were offering a $37.00-50 range, whilst one trader was seen bidding $36.75 as demand in the South continues to remain strong across early/mid June dates, setting up strong levels of activity into next week. The week rounded off with a tender out of Saldanha bay fixing to an operator at $27.19 for 10/14 Jun to China. The North continued to see strong demand throughout the week which was supported by high volumes of activity and a moderate tonnage. Monday saw one end user’s fronthaul tender from Narvik to Kandla fixed on a German operator’s vessel for 19/28 May at $43.50, which ran to 73.5k over 65 days and a $2.15mil score equivalent to $83k C9. Additionally, one operator fixed a couple of their transatlantic stems to start the week, from Nouadhibou to Arzew for tight end May dates in the high $12s which ran to around $56k adjusted for C8 duration as well as an Acu to Arzew cargo for 01/10 June. Tuesday saw one operator’s fronthaul stem from Drummond to South Korea holding a $48 offer for end June dates, but still remained, overall West African stems remained lucrative to North Atlantic stationed vessels. Demand continued to hold strong into an active Wednesday as one German owner was seen to make up the bulk of activity as they took a couple of stems. Fixing one backhaul cargo out of Saldanha Bay to Rotterdam for mid June at $17.00 which ran to around very low $20k's and a $1.42mil score for 65 day duration. Additionally, the same operator took a transatlantic stem for 20/29 May dates from Canada to France at a reported mid $22.50, which runs to around $56.7k as a Gibraltar RV. Momentum carried through into Thursday after the usual major out of Brazil promptly fixed their cargo at high $27.00's. On a transatlantic round voyage to Misurata for 08/17 June this ran to mid $40k's as a Gib RV, while on a ballaster this ran to around $16k adjusted. As the week came to a close on Friday, one miner’s fronthaul stem from Sept-Iles to China for forward late June dates attracted welcomed interest from moderate North tonnage. The basin continued to feel positive as demand remains strong and tonnage moderate heading into next week. items.parsed_text: Panam ax/Kamsarmax Report15th May 2026 ATL: FIRM PAC: FIRM MID EAST: FIRM Market Comments ATL SHORT: THE MARKET CLOSES THE WEEK ON A FIRMER FOOTING DESPITE A QUIETER HOLIDAY AFFECTED END TO THE WEEK. TONNAGE REMAINS TIGHT ACROSS BOTH THE NORTH AND SOUTH ATLANTIC, WHILE A STRONG PACIFIC MARKET CONTINUES TO DISCOURAGE BALLASTING. ALTHOUGH SOME PROMPT VESSELS OPEN OVER THE WEEKEND HAVE SHOWN MORE FLEXIBILITY, THE OVERALL SUPPLY/DEMAND BALANCE REMAINS SUPPORTIVE. PROVIDED CAPES HOLD THEIR RECENT GAINS AND CARGO FLOW REMAINS STEADY, THE ATLANTIC SHOULD CONTINUE TO TRADE AT ELEVATED LEVELS INTO NEXT WEEK, THOUGH AFTER THE RECENT SHARP MOVE HIGHER A PERIOD OF CONSOLIDATION WOULD NOT BE SURPRISING. PAC SHORT: THE PACIFIC MARKET STARTED THE WEEK ON A VERY FIRM FOOTING, WITH SENTIMENT INITIALLY REMAINING STRONGLY POSITIVE ON THE BACK OF HEALTHY CARGO ACTIVITY AND AGGRESSIVE FIXING ACROSS MOST ROUTES. EARLY IN THE WEEK, CARGO VOLUMES IMPROVED ACROSS THE BASIN WHILE TONNAGE REMAINED RELATIVELY BALANCED DESPITE A SLIGHT INCREASE IN AVAILABLE VESSELS, ALLOWING OWNERS TO MAINTAIN STRONG LEVERAGE. AUSSIE ROUNDS LED THE RALLY, WITH STRONG FIXING ACTIVITY PUSHING MOMENTUM HIGHER, WHILE NOPAC ALSO STRENGTHENED STEADILY WITH FRESH GRAIN AND COAL DEMAND SUPPORTING RATES. P3 CLIMBED SHARPLY THROUGH THE FIRST HALF OF THE WEEK AND WAS SEEN FIXING AROUND THE $24/25,000 LEVEL, WHILE P5 ALSO CONTINUED TO POST GAINS ALONGSIDE THE BROADER PACIFIC RALLY. HOWEVER, BY MIDWEEK ONWARDS, MOMENTUM BEGAN TO FADE AS CARGO ENQUIRY SLOWED NOTICEABLY ACROSS MOST REGIONS AND CHARTERERS STARTED PULLING BACK AFTER THE SHARP RUN UP IN RATES. FFAS ALSO TURNED SOFTER ACROSS THE CURVE DURING THE LATTER PART OF THE WEEK, REFLECTING GROWING CAUTION AROUND WHETHER THE MARKET COULD SUSTAIN SUCH ELEVATED LEVELS. ALTHOUGH INDICES REMAINED POSITIVE, DESPITE THE SOFTER SENTIMENT SEEN TOWARDS THE END OF THE WEEK, THE MARKET CONTINUED TO HOLD RELATIVELY FIRM OVERALL, WITH RATES MANAGING TO MAINTAIN MOST OF THE GAINS ACHIEVED EARLIER IN THE WEEK. ON THE SUPPLY SIDE, TONNAGE REMAINED RELATIVELY CONTROLLED, THOUGH THE BALANCE GRADUALLY BEGAN LOOSENING LATER IN THE WEEK AS CARGOES PUSHED FURTHER FORWARD AND FRESH ENQUIRY REMAINED LIMITED COMPARED TO FIRST HALF OF THE WEEK Recent Fixtures ATLANTIC MV MODEST SW (76/12) FLUSHING 15-19 MAY FIXED NCSA/SGP-JPN $27,500 MV AGIOS GEORGIOS S (75/12) KANDLA 16-17 MAY FXD ECSA/SGP-JPN GRAINS $19,500 PACIFIC MV TAI KINSHIP (84/21) CAM PHA 23/24 MAY FXD EAUS/SCHINA COAL $28,000 MV PACIFIC BLISS (81/25) DALIAN 21 MAY FIXED NOPAC GRAINS MID-HIGH $23,000SBaltic Routes Routes 08/05/26 15/05/26 P1A_82 Transatlantic RV 16,723 20,995 P2A_82 Cont-Far East 27,871 31,143 P3A_82 Transpacific RV 21,713 24,094 P4_82 Backhaul 15,119 16,548 P6_82 20,636 22,167 5TC Average 20,099 22,691 Physical Markets (All rates basis index type) Charterers Owners Transatlantic RV 21,000 23,000 + Cont-Far East 31,000 32,000 + Transpacific RV 23,000 25,000 + Backhaul 15,500 17,000 + Short period Atlantic* 23,500 25,500 + Short period Pacific 19,750 21,750 + 1 year Atlantic* 19,750 22,000 + 1 year Pacific 18,000 20,000 NC 2 years 16,750 18,000 + 3 years 16,000 17,000 + 5 years 15,000 16,500 + *Redelivery worldwide Panamax 5 TC Average $/day Approximate Tonnage Supply/Demand (<20 years, for guidance only) Atlantic Pacific UKC MED StLaw USEC USG ECSA SAFR ME FE SEASIAUSNP/BC SupplySpot/10 days 17 21 1 1 3 11 14 80 71 113 73 10/30 days 14 8 1 0 2 7 2 53 42 36 42 DemandSpot/10 days 0 0 1 0 0 0 0 1 5 10 8 10/30 days 1 3 1 3 5 9 0 1 5 13 8 Simpson Spence Young Ltd T: +44 (0)20 7977 7400 E: panamax@ssyglobal.comWhile reasonable care has been taken to ensure that the information in this publication is accurate, SSY can accept no responsibility for any errors or omissions or any consequences arising therefrom. OWNERS REMAINED FIRMLY IN CONTROL THROUGH WEDNESDAY, THOUGH A QUIETER END TO THE WEEK DUE TO ASCENSION DAY HOLIDAYS ACROSS EUROPE TOOK SOME MOMENTUM OUT OF THE MARKET AND LED TO MORE CAUTIOUS POSITIONING INTO THE WEEKEND. 1A THE TRANSATLANTIC MARKET SAW A SHARP RE-RATING THROUGH THE FIRST HALF OF THE WEEK, AS TIGHT TONNAGE AND STRONGER CAPE EARNINGS FORCED CHARTERERS TO PAY UP FOR PROMPT COVER. SHORTER MINERAL TRANSATLANTIC RUNS WERE CONCLUDED AS HIGH AS USD 24,000 BKI EQUIVALENT EX ALGECIRAS, WHILE LONGER DURATION TA BUSINESS TRADED MOSTLY IN THE MID USD 22,000’S TO LOW USD 23,000’S. ACTIVITY LEVELS WERE HEALTHY THROUGH WEDNESDAY, WITH OWNERS PUSHING OFFERS HIGHER AFTER EACH REPORTED FIXTURE. HOWEVER, AS THE WEEK PROGRESSED INTO THURSDAY, MOMENTUM SLOWED AND SOME VESSELS OPENING OVER THE WEEKEND BECAME MORE FLEXIBLE ON IDEAS IN ORDER TO SECURE COVER. EVEN SO, THE TONNAGE LIST REMAINS RELATIVELY TIGHT, AND THE MARKET CLOSES THE WEEK WELL ABOVE LAST FRIDAY’S LEVELS. 2A FRONTHAUL REMAINED THE STRONGEST ROUTE IN THE BASIN THIS WEEK. NCSA GRAINS CONTINUED TO DOMINATE THE MARKET, WHILE ADDITIONAL DEMAND FROM THE US INTO INDIA AND THE FAR EAST PROVIDED FURTHER SUPPORT. WITH VERY FEW SUITABLE VESSELS AVAILABLE, OWNERS WERE ABLE TO PUSH LEVELS AGGRESSIVELY HIGHER THROUGH MIDWEEK. WE SAW MULTIPLE NCSA/FEAST FIXTURES CONCLUDED AROUND USD 31,000 BKI EQUIVALENT EX ALGECIRAS, WHILE A PROMPT USEC/INDIA RUN WAS REPORTED AS HIGH AS USD 34,000 BKI EQUIVALENT EX ALGECIRAS. VOLUME WAS DECENT THROUGH THE FIRST HALF OF THE WEEK AND THE MARKET LOOKED GENUINELY TIGHT. HOWEVER, THE HOLIDAY SHORTENED END TO THE WEEK REDUCED LIQUIDITY AND A FEW PROMPT VESSELS OPEN OVER THE WEEKEND WERE REPORTED MORE NEGOTIABLE ON OFFERS. DESPITE THIS, THE UNDERLYING BALANCE REMAINS SUPPORTIVE WITH LIMITED TONNAGE AVAILABLE FOR MAY/1H JUNE DATES. P6 THE SOUTH ATLANTIC ALSO CONTINUED TO FIRM, THOUGH ACTIVITY LEVELS WERE MORE MEASURED COMPARED TO THE NORTH ATLANTIC. FIXTURES WERE REPORTED IN THE LOW TO MID USD 22,000’S P6 EQUIVALENT, WITH OWNERS BENEFITTING FROM A THIN BALLASTER LIST AND CONTINUED PACIFIC STRENGTH PREVENTING AN INFLUX OF OPEN TONNAGE. WHILE THE MARKET CONTINUES TO MOVE HIGHER, DEPTH OF BUYING HAS BEEN LESS IMPRESSIVE THAN IN PREVIOUS WEEKS. IN ADDITION, ULTRAMAX TONNAGE REMAINS COMPETITIVE, ALLOWING CHARTERERS WITH FLEXIBILITY TO SOURCE GEARED TONNAGE AT LOWER LEVELS. NEVERTHELESS, THE OVERALL SUPPLY SIDE REMAINS WELL MANAGED, AND THERE IS LITTLE SIGN OF OWNERS LOSING CONFIDENCE AT CURRENT LEVELS. Please click here to view our terms and conditions in section 6.2.Dry Cargo Report Panam ax/Kamsarmax Report15th May 2026 Pacific Comment PAC LONG: THE NOPAC MARKET PERFORMED STEADILY THROUGHOUT THE WEEK AND WAS ONE OF THE KEY SUPPORTIVE FACTORS BEHIND THE PACIFIC RALLY DURING THE EARLY STAGES. FRESH GRAIN AND COAL STEMS FOR EARLY JUNE, ALONGSIDE SOME REMAINING END MAY CARGOES, HELPED PUSH RATES HIGHER AND ALLOWED P3 TO ACHIEVE AROUND THE $24,000 LEVELS. HOWEVER, AS THE WEEK PROGRESSED, ENQUIRY BEGAN MOVING FURTHER FORWARD INTO MID-JUNE DATES AND THE AMOUNT OF FRESH CIRCULATION SLOWED. WHILE TONNAGE IN THE NORTH REDUCED TOWARDS THE END OF THE WEEK, THE SLOWER PACE OF FRESH DEMAND AND INCREASINGLY CAUTIOUS CHARTERER SENTIMENT RESULTED IN THE MARKET LOSING SOME MOMENTUM AFTER ITS STRONG START. AUSTRALIA WAS UNDOUBTEDLY THE STRONGEST PERFORMING REGION, WITH AGGRESSIVE FIXING ACTIVITY AND TIGHT PROMPT DEMAND DRIVING RATES SHARPLY HIGHER. EAUS ROUNDS ACHIEVED PREMIUM LEVELS, SUPPORTED BY STRONG EARLY JUNE DEMAND AND LIMITED PROMPT SUPPLY. HOWEVER, THE MARKET COOLED NOTICEABLY FROM MIDWEEK ONWARDS AS THE STRONG SECOND HALF MAY MOMENTUM FAILED TO PROPERLY ROLL INTO JUNE. FRESH CARGO ENQUIRY BECAME INCREASINGLY THIN, WITH ACTIVITY MAINLY LIMITED TO A HANDFUL OF CHINA STEMS FOR EARLY JUNE LAYCANS. DESPITE RATES REMAINING ELEVATED, SENTIMENT SOFTENED CONSIDERABLY AS CHARTERERS STEPPED BACK AND ADOPTED A MORE CAUTIOUS WAIT-AND-SEE APPROACH AFTER THE RAPID RISE SEEN EARLIER IN THE WEEK. INDO SAW SOME IMPROVEMENT AT THE START OF THE WEEK COMPARED TO PREVIOUS WEEKS, PARTICULARLY FOR LATER MAY DATES. HOWEVER, THE MARKET GRADUALLY LOST MOMENTUM THROUGH THE SECOND HALF OF THE WEEK AS INDONESIAN COAL ENQUIRY SLOWED SIGNIFICANTLY, ESPECIALLY INTO SOUTHEAST ASIA. CHINESE COAL TRADING ALSO BECAME QUIETER AMID VOLATILITY IN THE UNDERLYING COMMODITY MARKET, FURTHER WEIGHING ON SENTIMENT. BY FRIDAY, INDO DEMAND SEEMED THIN OVERALL, WITH FRESH CARGO COUNT REMAINING WELL BELOW LEVELS SEEN IN RECENT WEEKS. OVERALL, WHILE THE PACIFIC MARKET MANAGED TO HOLD ONTO MOST OF THE GAINS ACHIEVED EARLIER IN THE WEEK, THE BASIN CLEARLY LOST STEAM DURING THE LATTER HALF AS CARGO ENQUIRY SLOWED AND CHARTERERS RESISTED HIGHER LEVELS. UNDERLYING COAL FUNDAMENTALS REMAIN SUPPORTIVE, BUT WITH QUIETER CARGO VOLUMES, FLATTER FFAS AND INCREASINGLY CAUTIOUS SENTIMENT, THE MARKET LOOKS SET TO ENTER NEXT WEEK ON A MORE STABLE AND QUIETER FOOTING RATHER THAN CONTINUING THE SHARP UPWARD TRAJECTORY SEEN AT THE START OF THIS WEEK. THAT SAID, EVEN WITH SOFTER SENTIMENT DEVELOPING TOWARDS THE END OF THE WEEK, THE MARKET HAS STILL MANAGED TO HOLD ONTO ITS ELEVATED LEVELS RELATIVELY WELL, SUGGESTING UNDERLYING SUPPORT REMAINS FIRMLY IN PLACE FOR NOW. However, output stood 4.3% below the same period last year. As of 10 May, finished steel inventories of large and medium-sized enterprises in China also rose, up 9.4% from end-April to 16.9 Mt. The rise in stocks was faster than the lift in daily crude steel output since the Labour Day holiday (1-5 May) resulted in slack demand from downstream users. In the week to 8 May, the percentage of profitable Blast Furnace steel mills climbed 9.1 percentage points from the prior week to 60.2%, the highest since September 2025, MySteel data show. Meanwhile, Chinese iron ore imports lifted 0.7 Mt year-on- year to 103.8 Mt in April, despite lower shipments from Australia and heavy rain in Brazil. Trading Commentary Cape The Cape FFA curve was well supported today despite the index coming off another $1293, however the Atlantic physical market remains very tight still. The biggest move was on the June contract with 38650 paid, followed by the July with 35050 trading. The move on May was still significant, reaching a top of 42600. The May v Jun spread narrowed and weakened as a result, back down to 4000. Buying interest on the Q3 was similarly strong with a range of 32850-33350 and the Q4 31750-32100, with the Q3 v Q4 spread widening out to 1300. The Cal27 lacked liquidity today with a few clips printing marginally weaker down to 26600, before strengthening in response to the Q34 move. PMX PMX saw a relatively busy session for a Friday after a bank holiday for many, with activity mainly focused around the front of the curve. May stuck at 21500 in over 300 clips, June was again the main point of interest, trading between 21600 and 22050 finishing the day around 21800. while July traded in a tighter 21000–21300 range. August saw lighter activity at 20550, with September trading between 19800 and 19900. Further out, Q3 moved 20300–20650 closing around 20500, while Q4 traded in a narrower 18500–18700 range. The back end remained steady with Cal 27 staying around 15500. SMX + HANDY The down trend continued on smx paper today as we ended the week on a bearish note. Jun traded from 18750 to 18400 while q3 went from 18200 to 17900. Jul also Despite the move on the front the back end struggled to lose value with cal 27 having a conference rate of 13500, the same rate that was trading yesterday. items.parsed_text: Handysize/Supramax Report15th May 2026 63,500 Atlantic: FLAT Pacific: FLAT 38,000 Atlantic: FLAT Pacific: FLAT Atlantic Comment The Baltic Dry Index (BDI) shattered the 3,000-point barrier this week, reaching 3,189 by Wednesday, its highest level since late 2023. This rally is driven by a massive surge in Capesize earnings, which jumped over 5% to break $44,000 per day as miners aggressively push supply from the Atlantic. However, the market is becoming increasingly two tiered, while Capes are thriving, we are seeing limited cargoes on our segment as ports like Kamsar now ship primarily on Capes for fronthaul movements. Bunker prices continue to be a total rollercoaster, with VLSFO nearing the $1,000 threshold before swinging on volatile crude shifts, keeping a tight squeeze on margins. Despite this, the outlook through June remains firm, supported by double digit growth in global grain volumes and a recovery in coal demand as a hot Asian summer and weak monsoon loom. While a tactical ceiling from Panamax splits may soon cap the Capesize rally, the strong supply-push in iron ore and the ramp-up at Simandou should maintain sentiment until the usual seasonal lull in July. In the Mediterranean, we continue seeing a lack of fresh cargo enquiry. However, we are starting to observe a slight improvement across most routes both in E.Med and W.Med, with the latter showing somewhat firmer sentiment, likely supported by the stronger ECSA market, which currently offers more attractive returns despite the longer ballast distance. On the other hand, levels in the Continent remain healthier compared to the Med. However, this week we have seen some softening in the market due to the lack of fresh cargoes around, particularly scrap, which has put some pressure on rates. Unlike the resilient and firm Ultramax segment, the East Coast South America (ECSA) Handysize market has become increasingly fragmented this week, with fixture levels varying wildly. This lack of clear direction has resulted in a two-tier market where rates are dictated more by specific laycan dates and individual owner urgency than by any unified regional trend. With fewer active cargoes to absorb the remaining tonnage, the previous momentum has stalled, forcing a disconnect between those holding for last-done levels and those fixing lower to avoid becoming prompt. The ECSA Supramax market remains firm this week, but owners are finding themselves walking a tightrope between maintaining high benchmarks and overplaying their hand. There is a growing awareness that if Supramax owners pull the rope too much, the rate spread will narrow to the point where Panamax vessels become the more economical choice for charterers, potentially triggering a shift in vessel preference. This thin balance is further complicated by a widening discrepancy in earnings potential between vessel types; while Eco Ultramaxes are commanding a significant premium on Fronthaul runs compared to standard Supramaxes, the Transatlantic market remains a strong where both types continue to enjoy robust elevated levels. A tale of 2 halves this week.... With the Ascension day holiday yesterday the market ground to a halt, and today has been very quiet across the Atlantic basin. The USEC saw noticeably more activity with coal cargos leading the charge, its either feast of famine on that coast and it was a carbon feast this week. Runs to the Eastern Mediterranean proving the most lucrative given the weak state of the market there. Ultramax vessels have been fixing in the upper 20's in the latter part of this week. The USG has been somewhat quieter, levels have remained flat but well supported. A 61 dwt fixed a Japan grains at 25,000 midweek, and owners continue to ask for same levels for clean FH cargos with end May/June dates. Local grain runs in the have come off slightly. 19-21,000 usd per day can be achieved subject to redel port, perhaps indicating owners willingness to stay in the area with the expectation of a firmer June. Decent sentiment await us next week for a possible end May push which we've seen in the previous months end. Although the pace of the rally has moderated compared to the previous sharp run-up, the overall market structure remained healthy, with freight levels continuing to hold at elevated levels. Far East exports and the period market stayed active, providing solid support to the overall market, while the Southeast Asian coal sector remained relatively flat, though fixture levels continued to stay firm. The Indonesian coal market was relatively quiet this week, with limited fresh cargoes entering the market. However, as available tonnage in the region did not increase significantly, freight levels remained generally stable without any meaningful correction. Indo/SE Asia continued to be the most active regional route, with reported fixtures including a UMX open Singapore fixing around USD 19k for Indo/Philippines, and another UMX open Singapore fixing around USD 20.5k for Indo/Thai, indicating that short-haul coal trades continued to provide strong support. On the Indo/China route, Supramax demand remained relatively limited, as part of the cargo flow was handled by Panamax vessels, resulting in fewer visible fixtures in the market. Activity on the Indo/India route also softened slightly this week, with some owners preferring to keep their vessels within the Pacific basin in anticipation of stronger Far East export and period opportunities. The North Vietnam and South China region remained active this week. Long-haul cargoes such as clinker to Bangladesh and West Africa, as well as cement to the US Gulf and West Coast Central America, continued to provide stable support to the regional market. Reported fixtures included an SMX open South China fixing above USD 22k for clinker to Bangladesh, and a UMX open South China fixing above USD 24k for limestone to Bangladesh. For other long-haul trades, charterers increasingly showed preference for securing tonnage through period employment, with UMX short period levels in the South China–CJK area generally maintained above USD 21k. The nickel ore market was less active compared to previous weeks, with the overall pace of fixtures slowing somewhat, though shipment volumes remained steady. The NOPAC market also maintained a reasonable level of activity. Supported by strong northern export demand, freight levels remained firm. Market reports included a UMX on subs above USD 20k for a NOPAC round voyage, as well as a UMX open North China fixing around USD 19k for NOPAC round employment, indicating that market support remained solid. North China steel and general cargo exports continued to perform strongly. With tonnage in the Far East remaining tight, freight levels stayed elevated. General cargo demand to West Africa remained firm, with reports of a UMX open North China fixing around USD 24.5k dop to WAFR. Steel exports to Southeast Asia also maintained healthy levels, with rates generally staying within the high teens range, reflecting continued positive sentiment in the market. The Australian market remained stable this week, with cargo supply continuing to be released at a regular pace. Grain and salt from Western Australia, coal from Eastern Australia, and minerals from Northern Australia continued to move steadily, providing ongoing support to the regional market. Reported fixtures included a UMX open Cigading fixing around USD 22k+ for Australia/China iron ore, as well as an eco UMX fixing around USD 23k+ for Australia/China salt, with overall freight levels remaining firm. In the period market, confidence remained supported by the continued strength in the paper market. Although the spot market showed some signs of slowing, period levels remained firm overall. UMX short period fixing levels were generally maintained within the USD 21k–22k range, depending on vessel position, age, and specifications, reflecting owners’ continued confidence in the near- to medium-term market outlook. Overall, although the Pacific Supramax market did not continue the aggressive upward momentum seen previously, the underlying market structure has not weakened materially. Regional tonnage supply remains relatively tight, while Far East export demand and period activity continue to provide strong support. In the near term, with no significant inflow of open tonnage and cargo volumes remaining stable, the market is expected to continue trading at elevated levels. The weakness of the Rupee, which recently hit an all -time low against the US Dollar before recovering slightly, has further added pressure to sentiment from the Indian recyclers. At the same time, firm freight earnings continue to discourage owners from re- leasing older tonnage for recycling, keeping the supply of candidates limited. The situation is similar in Bangladesh, where local scrap levels have dropped by approximately USD 10 per lwt over the past week and, notably, closer to USD 30 per lwt during the course of the past month. Consequently, this has resulted in a more cautious sentiment being adopted by the ship recyclers. The recent heavy rains have also had an immediate effect on activity at the recycling yards and, with the monsoon season due to commence in earnest in the coming weeks, it is expected that current levels may remain stable alt- hough a softer demand environment could emerge should weather disrup- tions intensify. Even so, underlying appetite from the leading HKC -compliant yards remains present. Pakistan continues to be the most aggressive in terms of striving to acquire tonnage, as this sector is suffering from a shortage of imported scrap tradi- tionally supplied from the Gulf region. This has created a stronger require- ment internally although, in reality, there remains a shortage of buyers willing, or able, to increase price levels sufficiently enough to draw tonnage away from the Bangladesh market. With the monsoon delivery window gradually narrowing across the Sub - Continent, timing is also becoming an increasing consideration for both buy- ers and sellers alike. The vast majority of reported transactions are once again older sales, with various different countries being the recipients. Fresh sales are limited to the LPG carrier “Gas Crusader” (1,526 lwt), which has been committed for deliv- ery to Bangladesh at a reported level of USD 550 per lwt, a price clearly signi- fying the vessel’s high, albeit undisclosed, non -ferrous content. In addition, the Drillship “Valaris DPS -1” (38,568 lwt) has been sold on an as is basis in Indonesia on private terms. Geographically, Bangladesh remains the closest recycling destination, however the vast majority of offshore units continue to find their way towards India despite the considerably longer voyage, primarily due to the stronger appetite and specialist capabilities available within that sector.
